device.none: No devices yet. Tap + to add one.
pet.none: No pets yet. Add a pet to track feeding and weight.
settings.tz_hint: Daylight saving time is handled automatically. Enter schedule times in local time — the app converts to UTC for the feeder. Change takes effect after feeder reconnects.
settings.ha_bell_hint: Posts alerts to the Home Assistant notification bell.
settings.email_hint: Email-capable HA notify service (Gmail, SMTP, etc.). Select one to enable email alerts.
settings.email_to_hint: Fallback address used when a device has no email override set.
settings.mobile_hint: Mobile alerts are push notifications sent through the Home Assistant Companion app on your phone, not text messages. This is the default phone (mobile_app service) used when a device has Mobile enabled but no per-device service set.
settings.mqtt_hint: The add-on connects to this broker to receive device data. Create a dedicated broker user in Mosquitto for the add-on.
settings.local_audio_base_url_hint: A plain LAN address for this add-on, not the Home Assistant ingress link. Feeders fetch custom sounds directly over the network, they can't use your logged-in browser session. Required before you can push a custom sound to a feeder.
settings.audio_library_hint: Shared across all feeders. Push any of these to a specific feeder from its Maintenance tab.
settings.audio_library_empty: No sounds yet. Upload a file or record one below.
settings.audio_library_load_failed: Could not load the sound library.
settings.audio_delete_confirm: Delete "{name}"? Any feeder currently using it will keep playing it until a new sound is pushed.
settings.audio_record_insecure: Recording needs HTTPS (or localhost) to access your microphone. Home Assistant reached over plain HTTP can't do this — use Upload File instead.
settings.audio_upload_hint: Any common audio format works (MP3, WAV, M4A, etc.), it's converted automatically. Recording needs HTTPS or localhost access to your browser's microphone, which most home setups reached over plain HTTP don't have, Upload File works everywhere and is the reliable option.
settings.audio_record_empty: No audio was captured. Your browser may not support recording in this format, try a longer recording or use Upload File instead.
settings.mqtt_fail: ✗ MQTT connection failed — check host, port, username, and password
banner.pets: Add your pet(s) to enable feeding logs and RFID tracking.
banner.mqtt: Complete MQTT setup before adding devices. Enter the Mosquitto broker credentials in the MQTT tab, then tap Save & Test.
device_modal.delete_creds_confirm:
Also remove this device's credentials from the Mosquitto broker?

Keep them if you plan to re-add this device soon, or if another device uses the same login.

Removing them restarts the Mosquitto broker, which reboots all of your devices for a minute or two, so avoid doing it close to a feeding time.
overview.filter_indicator_hint: Turns off the fountain's red status LED. Only has a visible effect while the LED is actually lit for something (e.g. filter overdue) — it won't turn the light on by itself if nothing is wrong.
overview.light_schedule_enabled_hint: Confirmed working on real hardware. Likely the same choice as PetLibro's own "All Day" vs "Schedule" option for the fountain light.
overview.calibrate_scale_hint: Remove the water container from the fountain, then tap to zero the scale.
overview.calibrate_scale_container: Remove the container and try again
overview.no_pets: No pets assigned to this feeder. Tap Edit to assign a pet for feeding logs and tracking.
overview.display_text_hint: Text scrolls across the feeder display. Uppercase A-Z and 0-9, max 20 characters.
maint.min_drink_hint: 5g ≈ 1 tsp. Lower for kittens or small sips; raise if pump movement triggers false readings.
maint.feed_sounds_hint: Experimental. Push a custom sound clip to this feeder to play instead of the default chime. Requires Local Audio Base URL to be set in Settings.
maint.push_success: Sent! Listen for it at the next feed.
maint.feed_calibration_set: Calibrated: {grams}g per portion, based on your own measurements.
maint.feed_calibration_unset: Using the default 10g per portion. Calibrate against your own scale for a more accurate amount for your specific food.
feed_unit.heading: Food Amount Unit
feed_unit.hint: How feed amounts are shown for this feeder, like the Petlibro app's Food Amount setting. One portion is a fixed scoop, 1/12 cup or 20 ml, so cups and ml are exact. Grams and ounces depend on your food: they use 10 g per portion unless you calibrate below.
cal.title: Calibrate Feed Amount
cal.intro1: This will dispense 1 portion, {n} times. After each one, weigh what came out on your own kitchen scale and enter the grams. The average becomes this feeder's portion size everywhere amounts are shown.
cal.intro2: Since this feeder dispenses through a fixed-volume scoop rather than a scale, individual dispenses will vary a little, this gives a real average for your specific food instead of a flat guess.
cal.step_weigh: Step {step} of {total}: weigh what was just dispensed and enter the reading.
cal.unit_hint: One portion is only about 10g (0.35 oz), so grams is more accurate if your scale can show it. A scale that only reads to 0.1 oz can be off by a few grams.
maint.name_required: Enter a name for this sound first.
maint.desiccant_not_set: Not set — reset after first install
maint.bowl_not_set: Not set — record after first clean
log.no_intake: No intake recorded yet. Data accumulates as your pet drinks.
log.no_activity: No activity logged yet. Food dispensed and feeding sessions will appear here.
schedule.heading: Feeding Schedule
animed.title: Animation Editor
animed.library_hint: Pick one to copy it into the editor. Built-in ones can be changed and saved as your own. Yours are marked with a star in the picker.
animed.new_confirm: Start a new blank animation? Anything you have not saved will be lost.
animed.how: Click or drag the dots to light or clear them. Add a frame for each step of the animation, then press Send to Feeder.
animed.name: Animation name
animed.json_ph: Paste animation JSON here, then press Import
animed.share_hint: Export fills this box and downloads a file. Import accepts that JSON, or a list of frames where each frame is 7 text rows of 26 characters (# lit, . dark).
animed.exported: Exported. The JSON is in the box under Import / export if the download did not start.
animed.imported: Imported {n} frames into the editor. Save it to keep it.
animed.imported_saved: Imported {n} frames and saved "{name}" to your library.
animed.imported_unsaved: Imported {n} frames into the editor, but it was not saved (your library may be full, up to 20). Delete one and press Save.
animed.err_frames: Frames must be 1 to {n}, each with 7 numbers (or 7 text rows).
petname.heading: Pet name on tag read
petname.none: No pet assigned to this feeder
petname.hint: The feeder shows its stored pet name while it reads the pet's tag, then goes back to the idle screen. Petlibro Local never sends it on its own, so use this after you add or rename the pet. It sends the name of the pet assigned to this feeder.
anim.heading: LED animations
anim.hint: Plays on the feeder's idle LED screen and loops. Sending scrolling text or an icon again replaces it. Start with Display test to confirm all 7 rows light up.
hours.sound_hint: The feeder only makes its sounds (feeding beeps and any custom sound) inside this window. All day means always. Times are your local time.
hours.display_hint: The LED screen only lights inside this window. All day means always. The Show display switch turns it off completely. Times are your local time.
schedule.skip_today: Skip the next feeding of this plan (it runs normally after that)
schedule.run_all_hint: Turn off to pause every schedule at once (for example while you feed by hand). Your plans are kept and the feeder just stops following them until you turn this back on.
schedule.paused_note: All schedules are paused: the feeder has been sent an empty schedule and will not feed on its own. Your plans below are kept.
schedule.offline_toast: Plan saved (feeder offline — will sync on reconnect)
notif.missed_feed: Scheduled feed missed (nothing dispensed within 5 minutes)
notif.food_dispensed: Food dispensed (every feed, off by default)
notif.battery_low_hint: Set to 0 to disable. Any other value both enables this alert and sets the percentage it fires at.
notif.email_placeholder: Leave blank to use default from Settings
edit_device.title: Edit Device
edit_device.name: Display Name
edit_device.image_hint: Upload a custom photo. Leave blank to use the built-in variant image.
edit_device.eating_hint: RFID tag must be detected for at least this long to count as an eating session. Default: 30s.
edit_device.display_text_hint: Letters, numbers, spaces — up to 20 chars. Shown scrolling on the feeder screen.
edit_device.creds_hint: All fields are masked — safe to share screenshots.
add_device.title: Add Device
add_device.method_hint: How would you like to set up this device?
add_device.restart_warning: Setting up a device restarts the Mosquitto broker, which reboots all of your devices for a minute or two. Avoid doing this close to a feeding time.
add_device.auto_desc: Captures credentials automatically. Recommended for most users.
add_device.manual_desc: You already have the MQTT username and password.
add_device.auto_intro: We’ll stop the Mosquitto broker for up to 60 seconds while your device reconnects and hands us its credentials automatically.
add_device.auto_step1: 📱 Open the Petlibro app on your phone
add_device.auto_step2: 🔧 Tap your device → gear icon → Wi-Fi Settings → Reconnect
add_device.auto_step3: ✅ Walk through the Wi-Fi setup — no need to change anything, just confirm it
add_device.auto_hint: This forces the device to do a fresh connection so we can capture its credentials.
add_device.waiting_connect: Waiting for your device to connect...
add_device.waiting_hint: Open the Petlibro app and reconnect your device’s Wi-Fi now.
add_device.cred_warn: ⚠ Could not save credentials to Mosquitto automatically. You may need to add them manually in the Mosquitto broker settings after adding this device.
add_device.type_warn: ⚠ This serial number wasn't recognized as a supported device. Please select the correct device type manually below, if it's not in the list, this device isn't supported yet, please open a GitHub issue.
add_device.name: Display Name
add_device.serial_hint: Found on the label on the bottom of the device
add_device.timeout: Capture timed out. Power cycle the device and try again, or use Manual Setup.
add_device.capture_failed: Capture failed. Check the add-on logs for details.
crop.title: Crop Photo
crop.hint: Drag to reposition. Use the slider to zoom.
about.title: Help / About
about.debug_capture_hint: Downloads a rolling 24-hour log of raw device MQTT traffic, including any device this app doesn't recognize (marked UNRECOGNIZED). Collected continuously in the background, so it also catches devices that only check in occasionally. WiFi name and any local audio server URL are redacted, but this file still includes your device serial numbers, so please email it to github@mega-city.com rather than posting it publicly when reporting an unsupported or misbehaving device. Doesn't work in the Home Assistant Companion App's built-in browser, it can't save files this way, use a regular desktop or mobile browser instead.
polar.beta_notice: Early beta. The developer has no Polar to test on, so none of this has been run on real hardware by them. Stay near the feeder the first few times and keep the Stop button handy. Feeding plans are not managed here: the feeder keeps its own.
polar.suggests: This suggests the unit is {unit} (not applied automatically)
polar.unit_unknown_hint: The feeder takes a number for how long the door stays open, but it is not confirmed whether that number means seconds or minutes. Until you choose a unit here, Serve sends a test value of 1 (harmless either way). Run a test feed, watch how long the door stays open (the Last feed line shows the measured time), then pick the unit that matches: about 60 s means minutes, a few seconds means seconds.
polar.unit_known_hint: How long the door stays open when you press Serve here or in Home Assistant.
polar.confirm_serve: Serve plate {plate}? The feeder will turn to that plate and open the door for {duration} {unit}. Stay nearby and press Stop if anything looks wrong.
polar.confirm_test: Serve plate {plate} as a test feed? The unit of the door time is not set yet, so a value of 1 is sent. The feeder will turn to that plate and open the door briefly. Watch how long the door stays open.
polar.test_started: Test feed started. When it ends, the Last feed line shows how long the door stayed open.
polar.bad_duration: Enter a whole number from {lo} to {hi} {unit}.
